title: Understanding Principal Components
text: Principal components are derived from the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the centered design matrix X. The SVD of X is given by X=U*Σ*V**T, where U and V are orthogonal matrices and Σ is a diagonal matrix containing singular values.

title: Role of Σ in SVD
text: The Σ matrix in the SVD contains the singular values, which are crucial for determining the principal components. However, the principal components themselves are linear combinations of the original variables, represented by the columns of V.

title: Using U and $$V^T$$
text: Even if the Σ matrix is lost, the matrices U and $$V^T$$ can still provide valuable information. The columns of V (or rows of V**T) represent the directions of the principal components in the original feature space.

title: Finding Principal Components Without Σ
